title: Tenant e-Discovery and Retention Contract for Private Deploys
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
========
This page defines the customer-facing contract for tenant data retention, e-discovery, and legal-hold handling for Redwood private deployments (VPC, on-prem appliance, and air-gapped installs). The intent is to provide a prescriptive, auditable set of requirements operators and field teams must meet during onboarding, steady-state operations, and incident/legal requests. This contract sits alongside the telemetry classification and archival requirements in the customer requirements library.

Audience
--------
- Security and Compliance reviewers
- Field Operators (Operator Team)
- Customer SRE and Legal/Privacy contacts
- Solutions Engineers responsible for onboarding

Scope and Definitions
---------------------
- Tenant: a single logical customer namespace running on a private deployment.
- Retention boundary: the maximum timeframe for which event/trace/log/model artifact data must be retained in searchable form.
- E-discovery: customer-or-redwood-initiated requests to preserve and export data for legal, regulatory or investigatory purposes.
- Legal hold: an instruction to prevent deletion/rotation to meet an e-discovery request.
- Evidence package: curated bundle of artifacts (logs, model snapshots, alerts, traces) delivered for an investigation.

Contract Principles (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Minimal privilege and tenant-scoped exports: only data for requested tenant(s) is exported.
2. Immutable evidence preservation during legal hold: snapshots are write-protected and hashed.
3. Auditability: all e-discovery operations are logged with operator identity, timestamp, and verification checksum.
4. Customer choice for retention tiers: support for short, medium, and long retention tiers with documented cost/latency tradeoffs.

Retention Tiers and Defaults (operator-facing)
---------------------------------------------
| Tier | Retention (searchable) | Archive (cold) | Example use | Default for new tenants |
|------|------------------------|----------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| short | 7 days | 30 days | burst debugging, low sensitivity | NO |
| medium | 30 days | 365 days | standard support investigations | YES |
| long | 365 days | 7 years | regulatory investigations, e-discovery | BY CONTRACT |

Notes:
- Searchable data = immediately available in the query interface and for forensic tools.
- Archive (cold) = encrypted object storage with retrieval window SLA (see Retrieval SLAs).

Storage, Encryption, and Integrity Controls
------------------------------------------
- All retained telemetry and artifacts must be encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS when requested. Use AES-256 for object encryption and TLS1.3 for transport.
- Evidence snapshots must be stored with an immutable object store policy (WORM) where supported. On systems without native WORM, apply a metadata-based isolation and operator process checklist to simulate immutability.
- Each evidence package will include SHA256 checksums for binary artifacts and signed manifest.json containing: operator, customer request id, timestamp, and retention tier.

Audit and Access Controls
------------------------
- Every e-discovery action (preserve, export, release) generates an immutable audit event with: operator_id, operator_ip, request_ticket, requested_tenants, assets_included, checksums. Audit logs must be retained for at least 2x the longest retention tier.
- Access to e-discovery endpoints must be RBAC-protected. Minimum roles: Operator, Operator-Approver, Legal-Viewer, Customer-Supplemental-Viewer.

Procedures: Onboarding (operator checklist)
-----------------------------------------
1. Confirm customer retention selection and sign the retention SLA appendix in the onboarding contract.
2. Configure tenant retention profile in Operator Console: set searchable_tier, archive_bucket, kms_key_arn (if customer-managed).
3. Run acceptance test: execute retention-verification job:

   ```bash
   redwood-ops retention-verify --tenant=acme-corp --expected-tier=medium 
   ```

   Expected output: PASS with sample artifact manifest.
4. Ensure alerting is configured: retention-rotation-fail and archive-retrieval-failure alerts to oncall and customer success.
5. Record configuration snapshot and sign-off in the evidence vault (s3://redwood-evidence/onboarding-snapshots/<tenant>).

Procedures: Legal Hold Activation (operator procedure)
----------------------------------------------------
1. Receive legal hold request via the ticketing system (JIRA ticket pref: ED-<nnnn>).
2. Operator-Approver verifies ticket and customer identity (2-factor verification).
3. Execute preserve operation: create an immutable snapshot of all searchable data for affected tenant(s). Example CLI: 

   ```bash
   redwood-ops ed-preserve --tenant=acme-corp --ticket=ED-1243 --note="preserve before infra upgrade"
   ```

4. The preserve command will:
   - snapshot current KV cache manifests, generation_id, model artifact sha256, runtime logs for last N hours (configurable).
   - tag preserved objects with legal_hold:ED-1243 and set immutability flag.
5. Post-preserve, the system will schedule checksum verification in 1 hour and emit audit event.

Procedures: Evidence Export and Packaging
----------------------------------------
1. Approver validates scope and signs export parameters (time range, models, traces).
2. Generate export manifest and preflight: 

   ```bash
   redwood-ops ed-export --tenant=acme-corp --ticket=ED-1243 --from=2026-02-01 --to=2026-02-10 --assets=logs,traces,models --out=/tmp/acme-evidence
   ```

3. Evidence is packaged into a gzipped tarball with manifest.json and checksums. Tarball is staged to customer's archive_bucket.
4. For private/onprem: when network egress is disallowed, the evidence package will be burned to a signed removable artifact (USB / encrypted disk) following chain-of-custody workflow.

Retrieval SLAs and Cost Considerations
-------------------------------------
- Searchable retrieval: immediate for short and medium tiers.
- Archive retrieval: 4 hours for medium, 24 hours for long tier (default). Operators must publish actual retrieval SLA per customer contract.
- Long-term archival retrieval requests may incur retrieval fees; fees and processes must be documented in the contract appendix.

Verification and Test Suite (operator-run)
-----------------------------------------
Regular tests (automated):
- daily: retention-rotation-health (ensures objects with expiry have correct TTL tags)
- weekly: evidence-snapshot-integrity (verify checksums against stored manifests)
- monthly: legal-hold-drill (simulate a preserve and export for a non-production tenant)

Example retention-rotation-health check (pseudo-query):

   SELECT object_key, ttl_tag, expiry_date FROM tenant_archive WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-corp' AND now() < expiry_date + interval '7 days';

Acceptable thresholds:
- retention-rotation-health PASS rate >= 99.5%
- evidence-snapshot-integrity PASS rate >= 99.9%

Escalation and Ownership
------------------------
- Primary: Field Operator Team (eng-private-deployments/operators). Contact: oncall-operators@redwood.com.
- Secondary: Security Compliance (security-compliance@redwood.com).
- Legal liaison: assigned per-customer; Solutions Engineer must record contact during onboarding.

Data Minimization and Redaction
-------------------------------
- Exported evidence should exclude unrelated tenant data. Operators must use automated filters and a manual reviewer step for PII redaction where required.
- For model artifacts that contain customer data, the team must provide a redaction report describing fields redacted and justification.

Forensics and Chain of Custody
-----------------------------
- Evidence packages must include operator signatures (GPG or KMS-signed manifest) and a chain-of-custody log: exported_by, exported_to, transport_method, handover_receipt.
- In air-gapped installs, use a dual-operator handoff (two operators present) and record video evidence where permitted by customer contract.

Rollback and Reversal of Legal Hold
----------------------------------
1. Legal Hold may only be released by a Legal-Viewer or Operator-Approver after ticket closure.
2. Release procedure: `redwood-ops ed-release --ticket=ED-1243 --approver=ben.rodriguez`
3. On release: system will mark preserved objects as eligible for normal rotation after a configurable cool-down (default 14 days) and will emit an audit event.

Compliance Evidence Package Contents (minimum)
--------------------------------------------
- manifest.json (signed)
- operator_signatures.asc (or kms_signature.txt)
- searchable logs (time window)
- control-plane traces and request_ids
- model-revision.tar.gz with manifest and sha256
- storage checksums and retrieval proofs

Appendix: Typical CLI snippets and samples
-----------------------------------------
- Verify retention mapping for tenant:
  ```bash
  redwood-ops tenant-show --tenant=acme-corp --fields=retention_profile,archive_bucket,kms_key
  ```
- Force integrity recheck for evidence snapshot:
  ```bash
  redwood-ops evidence-verify --snapshot-id=ss-20260217-0001
  ```
